{
  "claim": "https://w3id.org/delphi/resource/claim/fisher-ftns",
  "source": "network",
  "nanopubs": [
    "https://w3id.org/np/RAtLFqIIyu4r-GlMcBEfmDtbV-CHwWxQ49gVMtHIX6r48"
  ],
  "fields": {
    "rdf:type": [
      "https://w3id.org/delphi/ontology/Claim",
      "https://w3id.org/delphi/ontology/TestableHypothesis"
    ],
    "rdfs:label": "Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection (partial-change form)",
    "dct:description": "The rate of increase in mean fitness of a population due to natural selection equals its additive genetic variance in fitness at that time.",
    "rdfs:seeAlso": [
      "https://doi.org/10.1016/0040-5809(89)90028-2",
      "https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1469-1809.1972.tb00764.x"
    ],
    "dct:source": "Ronald A. Fisher (1930) The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection",
    "delphi:context": "Assumptions: the 'partial change' holds average effects of alleles and the environment fixed (Price 1972, Ewens 1989); V_A is the additive genetic variance in fitness. Formal status: proved in this partial-change reading. Read as a claim about the total change in mean fitness it is false under dominance, epistasis, frequency dependence or a changing environment.",
    "delphi:hypothesisType": "model-theorem",
    "delphi:proposedTest": "In a pedigreed wild population or an experimental-evolution line, estimate the additive genetic variance in relative fitness (animal model) and compare it with the observed per-generation response of breeding values for fitness, separating the selection term from environmental deterioration.",
    "skos:notation": "\\Delta_{NS}\\bar{w} = V_A(w)/\\bar{w} (discrete generations); \\left.\\frac{d\\bar{m}}{dt}\\right|_{NS} = V_A(m) for Malthusian fitness m"
  },
  "assessments": []
}
